detail.longDescription: It appears there are several different ways to select data with the SQLAlchemy ORM: Using session.query.filter() : rows = session.query(MyTable).filter( MyTable.column1 == value1, MyTable.column2 == value2 ).all() Using session.query.filter_by() : rows = session.query(MyTable).filter_by( column1=value1, column2=value2 ).all() Using select.where() : statement = select(MyTable).where( MyTable.column1 == value1, MyTable.column2 == value2 ) rows = session.execute(statement) And possibly even more ways that I am overlooking. Is there reason to prefer one of these methods over another? I imagine some of them are "the old way of doing it", to provide backward compatibility with older versions of SQLAlchemy. What is the currently accepted best practice?
